hints.text: Ignore the decimal point for a second: what is $6 \times 7$?
$6 \times 7 = 42$. The factor $0.6$ has one decimal place, so the answer needs one too.
Put the point one place from the right: $4.2$.

explanation: Multiply first as if there were no decimal point: $6 \times 7 = 42$.
Count decimal places in the factors. $0.6$ has one and $7$ has none, so the product needs one decimal place.
Place the point one digit from the right of $42$ to get $4.2$.
So $0.6 \times 7 = 4.2$, which makes sense because it is a bit more than half of $7$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Does it make sense?
steps: The decimal $0.6$ is a bit more than one half, and half of $7$ is $3.5$, so the answer must be a bit more than $3.5$.
The extra bit is one tenth of $7$, which is $0.7$, because $0.6 = 0.5 + 0.1$.
Add the half and the extra tenth together: $3.5 + 0.7 = 4.2$.
